summary: Set 108 Session 3 of 4 cut the tutorial estate down to the ladder: one task -> one module -> three modules. It is a pure removal-and-reconciliation pass, and its first act was to discharge the blocking precondition S2's close put on it -- confirm BY READING that ownership routing actually landed in `three-module-pipeline.md` before deleting the part that used to own it. It had: Step 4 'Route reviews by ownership', lines 653-686, carrying BOTH the GitHub CODEOWNERS form and the Azure DevOps 'Automatically included reviewers' equivalent, exactly as S1's ruling R4 required. A link grep would have passed either way, which is why the precondition existed. TRIM: `adopt-dabbler.md` lost Part 5 (teammate + composing module) and Part 6 (review/merge/cleanup) entirely, 459 -> 333 lines. Part 6 fell with Part 5 because it existed only to review Part 5's module; Part 4 already carries open-PR -> merge -> Finalize merged set for the reader's own module, so no procedure was lost from the tutorial. The consequential repairs mattered more than the deletion (L-065-1: a consistency fix is global, not point-local): the intro's 'two-module' promise, the 'this guide currently carries the team workflow too' note, branch protection renumbered 'stage N of 3' -> 'of 2' with stage 3's fact restated once at stage 1 (adopt-dabbler OWNS branch protection, and the new tutorial does not cover the approvals count), 'Parts 3-5' -> 'Parts 3-4', two prose forward-references to Part 5, and the closing five-item check rewritten from greeter+app to greeter alone. The stated completion time was cut from 'about two hours' to 'about an hour and a half' AND explicitly labelled an estimate rather than a stopwatch reading -- two of six parts were removed, and leaving the old number would have been a stale inherited claim (L-064-8). VIDEO: `docs/tutorials/adopt-dabbler-video/` deleted, 9 files, operator-sanctioned in the spec. Its single live inbound link went with the 'On camera' bullet. On the marker count the spec was imprecise and the verifier was right: there were SIX `*(scene N)*` heading markers (one per Part 1-6) plus ONE video-link bullet, not seven markers -- 4 stripped from surviving headings, 2 removed with their parts, 1 bullet removed. Set 107's activity log and change log mention the folder historically and were NOT touched. LINKERS: of the spec's seven, five were edited (README.md, quick-start.md, module-reorganization.md, module-team-hello-world.md, release-and-recovery.md), one was the trim itself, and ONE WAS DELIBERATELY NOT EDITED. `hello-world.md` makes no two-module promise, and adding the new tutorial to it would have turned CI RED: tutorial_gate's _BANNED_TERMS forbids 'pipeline', 'repository' and 'teammate' in the first-run document, and the new tutorial is titled 'Three modules, one pipeline'. The ladder still reads correctly as a chain, each rung naming the next. THE UNPLANNED FINDING, operator-adjudicated: CI was ALREADY RED on master when this session started, at S2's close (be4d3b8). `tutorial_gate.py`'s _COMMAND_RE had no '.' in its character class, so it captured 'Dabbler: Open modules' out of the correct text 'Dabbler: Open modules.yaml' and then correctly reported that truncated string as a command that does not exist. The tutorial was right and the gate was wrong; S2's tutorial is simply the first document in the repo to name that command, which is what surfaced the latent defect. Fixed by allowing a dot only when a letter or digit follows it, so a dotted title is captured whole while a sentence-final period stays outside the match. Two regression tests added (L-069-1). This sits outside the spec's S3 Touches list and its 'no new router code' non-goal -- which is aimed at product gaps the WALK reveals, not at a gate this set itself turned red two commits earlier. It was disclosed in the conventions block, the cross-provider verifier independently flagged that disclosure does not authorize scope expansion, and THE OPERATOR APPROVED IT, choosing to keep it as its own commit so it stays independently revertable. VERIFICATION: one round, VERIFIED, 0 blocking findings, from a two-way discovery fan-out (both calls gpt-5-6, anthropic auto-excluded). Eight nits total across the two calls, none blocking. Two were accepted and fixed AFTER the verified round, both in text this session had already touched: README still promised 'a reviewed pull request' when the trimmed solo walk requires zero approvals (now 'a gated pull request'), and the new regression test was FAIL-OPEN -- it asserted only the absence of a violation, which a regex that ignored dotted titles entirely would also satisfy, so it now asserts the capture equals 'Open modules.yaml' exactly. Gate and its 85 tests re-run green after both fixes. Three nits recorded as adjudicated-minor without change: the deleted VIDEO SCRIPT (never the tutorial) held the only procedure for actively proving a direct push to main is rejected -- re-homed to the owed adopt-dabbler walk rather than invented here; the conventions block asserted grep/gate/pytest results without pasting the command output; and 'this session creates nothing' referred to product deliverables while the session does add lifecycle machinery (s3-conventions.md). SUITE: GREEN -- 3143 passed, 6 skipped, 8 deselected in 48m55s, via the invocation pytest.ini names as the pre-commit one (the e2e mark deselected). Plus tutorial_gate.py exit 0 and its own 85 tests green, re-run after the two post-verification nit fixes. The suite is simply SLOW on Windows, not hung: an earlier full run was stopped at 35 minutes on the mistaken read that it had stalled, when the real cause is git subprocess spawn overhead across ~3000 tests. Worth knowing before a future session kills a healthy run: budget ~50 minutes, and note that the e2e mark drives start_session/close_session against real git repos in tmpdirs and has nothing to do with the Copilot seat.

reason.specifics: S4 is set-terminal and carries six deliverables: the walk evidence, the defect fixes the walk forces, the UAT checklist, change-log.md, the Step 9 guidance reorganization review, and the advisory path-aware critique. Two of those are the hardest things in this repo to get right at any tier. First, the UAT checklist is quality-gated on VOLUME, not just wording: the operator's standing bar from Set 107 S3 is ~4 items / ~2.6k chars derived from the acceptance criterion, after 9 items / 15k chars was judged 'daunting and tedious' -- writing less while losing nothing is high-effort work. Second, the walk's defects must be fixed WITHOUT re-opening settled design: S1's rulings R1-R9 closed VERIFIED across eight rounds, and a cheaper tier that 'fixes' a stall by re-litigating owner-in-slug or the two deliberately distinct 400s would undo the most expensive session in the set. Carry into S4: capture the walk against a fixed template -- {Part, Step, Action, Expected, Actual, Defect/Stall} -- rather than freeform notes; that is the one recommendation adopted from the step-3.5 analyst, and it improves on Set 107's freeform capture. Per-part elapsed time is required by the spec and MUST be labelled an estimate unless a stopwatch was really held. The analyst's own next_orchestrator named engine 'bedrock', which is not an engine in this repo -- the second consecutive session in which the step-3.5 analyst emitted an out-of-catalogue identifier -- so the recommendation is restated on its merits. Second choice if the operator prefers provider diversity: openai / gpt-5-6, effort high.
